title: Max Difference You Can Get From Changing an Integer
summary: Given an integer, apply a digit replacement operation twice to create two new numbers.
statement: Given an integer, apply a digit replacement operation twice to create two new numbers. Each operation involves replacing all instances of a chosen digit with another. Return the greatest difference between these two resulting numbers, ensuring neither has leading zeros.
constraints: For each of two values, replace every occurrence of one chosen digit with another digit.
Neither result may have a leading zero; return the largest possible difference.
hints: To maximize, replace the first digit not already nine and all its repeats with nine.
To minimize, change a non-one leading digit to one.
If the leading digit is one, change the first later digit outside zero/one to zero.
The earliest differing decimal position dominates every later choice, proving each greedy remap.
editorial: The earliest differing decimal position dominates every later choice, proving each greedy remap.

tests.explanation: Changing 5 to 9 gives 999 and changing 5 to 1 gives 111, for difference 888.
The maximum remains 9 and the minimum is 1, giving eight.
